issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize both orders and the stock in the SealSaloon constructor (a no-arg constructor), but elsewhere the specification requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across all instances. Initializing a static (and final) stock in an instance constructor is contradictory and may confuse students about where and how to initialize the shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: either (A) require stock to be a static (shared) attribute and state that it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor), or (B) make stock an instance (non-static) final field and require it to be initialized in the no-arg constructor. Updating the problem statement to remove the sentence that says to initialize stock in the constructor (or to explicitly explain static initialization) will resolve the contradiction.

issues.description: The UML and textual specification declare checkOrderReady() as returning void, but the provided solution implements checkOrderReady() with a boolean return type. This mismatch between the specification and the solution's method signature could confuse students about the intended method signature and return value.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either update the problem statement/UML to indicate checkOrderReady() returns boolean (and document the meaning of the return value), or change the solution to implement checkOrderReady() as void while preserving the same behavior (e.g., remove the boolean return and keep internal logic). Ensure tests and examples match the chosen signature.
